title: Active Model Adaptation Under Unknown Shift

problem.claim: Applications face distribution shift under unforeseen open-world conditions, while adaptation resources are often constrained.

gap.claim: The paper frames resource-constrained adaptation under unknown shift as a problem requiring active model adaptation.

contributions.claim: A generalization analysis of active model adaptation for distribution shift is presented.
Auto is presented as a systemic solution with distribution tracking, sample selection, and model adaptation.
Empirical studies evaluate nine existing active strategies on diverse real-world datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present a generalization analysis and the Auto solution for active model adaptation under distribution shift.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Theoretical analysis reports an improvement in generalization error from O(1/N) to O(1/N) with only a few queried samples.
The authors report that Auto remarkably outperforms all baselines in empirical studies.

narrative_sequence.summary: Machine learning commonly relies on fixed data distributions, but unforeseen situations can cause distribution shift.
Resources available for mitigating distribution shift are often constrained.
The paper studies active model adaptation theoretically and empirically for resource-constrained adaptation under unknown shift.
Auto combines shifted-distribution detection, core-set-based sample selection, and model updating with newly queried labels.
The authors report evaluations against nine existing active strategies on diverse real-world datasets, with Auto outperforming all baselines.

source_observation.claim: The proposed system tracks distribution shifts, selects informative samples under a labeling budget, and adapts the model using newly queried labels.

interpretation.claim: A staged adaptation workflow can allocate limited labeling resources toward samples most relevant to detected shift.

application.claim: Use shift detection followed by budget-aware informative sampling before updating a deployed model when distribution changes are unknown.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish effectiveness outside the reported evaluation setting or specify the required labeling and computation budgets.

unknowns: The stated theoretical rate is written as an improvement from O(1/N) to O(1/N), so the intended distinction is unclear.
The abstract does not specify the queried-sample count, dataset identities, evaluation metrics, or baseline identities.
The abstract does not provide formal assumptions, theorem conditions, or implementation details.
